intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the dark countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to chase the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to maximize your chances of witnessing the phenomenon. Hot chocolate and warm blankets included.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, a silica mud mask ritual, and a swim-up bar with Icelandic craft beer. A quintessential hot spring experience set against dramatic lava fields.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest natural swimming pool, a rustic geothermal hot spring dating back to 1891. Watch small geysers bubble nearby while soaking under open skies. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and wonderfully authentic.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and Viking heritage on a guided walking tour. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup, fermented shark, and fresh langoustine. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and the colorful old harbour district.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's breathtaking rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a natural geothermal hot spring soak at the end of the trail. Witness vivid green, red, and yellow volcanic landscapes unlike anywhere else on Earth.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives late at night
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives late at night
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the budget-friendly Flybus shuttle (~3,000 ISK) to Reykjavík and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. If skies are clear, step outside briefly to scan for the Northern Lights from the beachfront — January nights offer excellent aurora opportunities.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the Keflavík airport arrivals hall (soup or sandwich, ~1,500–2,000 ISK) before boarding the shuttle

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first night light — you will be jet-lagged. Download the Icelandic Met Office app (vedur.is) to track aurora forecasts throughout your trip. Exchange a small amount of currency or confirm your card works on arrival. January temperatures can be around -2°C to 4°C — dress in warm layers immediately upon landing.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in to recover from travel. After a slow start, enjoy a self-prepared or hostel-style breakfast at the resort. Walk along the beachfront near the Aegean Bliss Resort to get your bearings and enjoy the dramatic Icelandic winter coastline. Daylight in January is limited (roughly 10:00–16:00), so plan to be outdoors during these hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus or walk to explore the nearest town center. Visit a local supermarket such as Bónus or Krónan to stock up on budget groceries — bread, skyr, instant oatmeal, fruit, and snacks — to save money on meals throughout the trip. Stroll along the harbor area and admire the rugged coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and cook a simple meal with groceries. After dark (around 17:00), bundle up and head to the beachfront for your first serious Northern Lights watch. January darkness lasts nearly 20 hours, maximizing aurora viewing time. Check the aurora forecast app for KP index — anything above 3 is promising.

meals.breakfast: Skyr with granola and coffee from the resort or a nearby café (~800 ISK)
meals.lunch: Bónus supermarket finds — rye bread with smoked salmon or cheese (~600 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked pasta with canned tomato sauce and vegetables from the supermarket (~700 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January daylight is extremely limited — roughly 5–6 hours. Plan all outdoor sightseeing between 10:00 and 16:00. The long nights are your biggest advantage for Northern Lights hunting. Set an aurora alert on your phone.

day_by_day.morning: Head out early (by 10:00) to make the most of daylight. Visit the famous Golden Circle on a budget by joining a shared group tour (~8,000–10,000 ISK) or renting a small car with fellow travelers. First stop: Þingvellir National Park — walk the rift valley between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Free entry to the park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle route to the Geysir Geothermal Area — watch Strokkur erupt every 5–10 minutes for free. Then drive to Gullfoss Waterfall, one of Iceland's most iconic cascades. Bring crampons or grippy boots as paths can be icy in January.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by 17:00 before full darkness. Warm up with a hot drink and dinner. By 19:00–21:00, head outside or to a dark spot near the coast for Northern Lights viewing. The Golden Circle's rural areas away from Reykjavík light pollution are ideal if you have a car.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal with banana and coffee at the resort (~500 ISK self-prepared)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket — rye bread sandwiches, apple, and a thermos of hot coffee (~700 ISK)
meals.dinner: Budget bowl of lamb soup (kjötsúpa) at a local diner or self-cooked at resort (~1,500 ISK dine out or ~800 ISK self-cooked)

day_by_day.notes: Shared Golden Circle tours are the most budget-friendly option if you don't have a car. Book in advance through budget tour operators like Gray Line or Reykjavík Excursions. Dress in thermal base layers, mid-layers, and a windproof outer shell — Golden Circle in January is very cold and windy.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — one of Iceland's oldest and most affordable geothermal pools (~2,800 ISK entry). Soak in the natural hot spring surrounded by geothermal steam vents and a small geyser. This is far cheaper than the Blue Lagoon and equally beautiful. Travel by shared shuttle or car rental.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the lagoon, explore the small village of Flúðir and the surrounding rural Icelandic landscape. Stop at a local greenhouse or farm store to pick up fresh tomatoes and cucumbers — Iceland grows produce in geothermal greenhouses year-round. Head back toward the resort in the early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and warm up at the resort after the hot spring soak. Prepare a hearty dinner with fresh greenhouse vegetables. Check aurora forecast — if KP index is favorable, drive or walk to a dark coastal spot for Northern Lights viewing. Bring a tripod if you have a camera for long-exposure aurora photography.

meals.breakfast: Skyr parfait with berries and granola at the resort (~600 ISK self-prepared)
meals.lunch: Soup and bread at a café near the Secret Lagoon (~1,800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Homemade vegetable stir-fry with rice using greenhouse produce (~900 ISK self-cooked)

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is a fantastic budget alternative to the Blue Lagoon. Book entry tickets online in advance. Water temperature is around 38–40°C — blissful in January cold. Bring a towel and swimsuit. Lockers are available on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to the South Coast of Iceland. Start at Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — you can walk behind the curtain of water (weather permitting in January, as the path may be icy). Entry is free; only parking costs ~700 ISK. Nearby, visit Gljúfrabúi hidden waterfall, tucked inside a canyon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east along the South Coast to Skógafoss Waterfall — a massive 60-meter-wide cascade. Climb the staircase alongside it for panoramic views (free). Then drive to Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach near Vík — one of Iceland's most dramatic landscapes, with black volcanic sand, basalt columns, and sea stacks. Be cautious of sneaker waves.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the resort as darkness falls. Stop at the small town of Vík for a hot bowl of soup at a local café before the drive back. Once home, monitor aurora forecasts and head out if conditions are good — the South Coast away from city lights offers excellent aurora views.

meals.breakfast: Rye bread with butter and jam, coffee at the resort (~400 ISK self-prepared)
meals.lunch: Packed sandwiches and thermos of hot soup eaten at Skógafoss (~600 ISK self-prepared)
meals.dinner: Fish and chips or lamb soup at a casual restaurant in Vík (~2,200 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: South Coast roads in January can be icy or snowy — drive slowly and check road conditions at road.is before departing. Reynisfjara Beach is beautiful but dangerous — never turn your back to the ocean. Sneaker waves have claimed lives here. Stay well back from the water's edge.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely morning at the resort. Take a peaceful winter walk along the beachfront, listening to the waves and watching for seabirds. Bring a hot thermos of coffee and enjoy the moody Icelandic winter atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local geothermal swimming pool (sundlaug) — every Icelandic town has one and they are extremely affordable (~1,000 ISK entry). These community pools are heated by geothermal energy and include hot pots at varying temperatures. A true local experience. Ask the resort for the nearest pool location.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a budget-friendly Icelandic-inspired dinner at the resort — skyr-marinated chicken or baked fish with potatoes and vegetables. After dinner, head out for a dedicated Northern Lights hunt. Drive away from any artificial lights and park in a dark field or coastal area. Bring warm blankets, hot drinks in a thermos, and patience.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes with Icelandic butter and jam (~500 ISK self-prepared)
meals.lunch: Skyr, crackers, cheese, and apple at the resort (~600 ISK self-prepared)
meals.dinner: Baked cod with boiled potatoes and butter — classic Icelandic budget meal (~1,000 ISK self-cooked)

day_by_day.notes: Local geothermal pools (sundlaugar) are one of the best budget experiences in Iceland and a genuine window into local culture. Icelanders of all ages use them daily. Swimsuit and towel required. Some pools have waterslides and steam rooms included in the entry price.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula if budget allows for a car rental or shared tour. Visit Snæfellsjökull National Park — the glacier-topped volcano made famous by Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Walk along the volcanic lava fields and black sand beaches of Djúpalónssandur.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming fishing village of Arnarstapi with its dramatic coastal cliffs, sea arches, and bird colonies. Walk the coastal path to Hellnar (about 2.5 km) for stunning cliff scenery. Stop at the small café in Hellnar for a warming bowl of soup — one of Iceland's most scenic café locations.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back to the resort. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is excellent for Northern Lights viewing due to low light pollution — if aurora activity is forecast, pull over at a dark spot on the peninsula before heading home. Return to the resort by 21:00.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal with raisins and honey at the resort (~400 ISK self-prepared)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Djúpalónssandur beach (~600 ISK self-prepared)
meals.dinner: Hearty fish soup at the Hellnar café (~2,000 ISK) or self-cooked dinner at resort on return

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is about 2–3 hours from Reykjavík. The peninsula road (Route 54) can be challenging in winter — check road.is and only proceed if conditions are safe. A 4WD vehicle is recommended. Shared tours are available from Reykjavík if you prefer not to drive.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning exploring Reykjavík city on a budget. Walk to Hallgrímskirkja Church — Iceland's most iconic landmark. Admire the exterior for free or pay ~1,000 ISK to take the elevator to the top for panoramic city views. Stroll Skólavörðustígur street, lined with colorful houses and independent shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free outdoor Sun Voyager sculpture on the Reykjavík waterfront — a stunning steel dreamboat overlooking the bay. Walk along the harbor promenade. Browse the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends, ~200 ISK entry) for cheap Icelandic woolens, vintage items, and local snacks. Try hákarl (fermented shark) if you're feeling adventurous — vendors often offer free samples.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavík's budget-friendly food scene. Visit Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — Iceland's most famous hot dog stand operating since 1937. One hot dog costs ~500 ISK and is considered a national institution. Walk the lively Laugavegur street and window-shop. Return to the resort by late evening.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at a local Reykjavík bakery such as Brauð & Co (~900 ISK)
meals.lunch: Hot dog at Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur with mustard, remoulade, and crispy onions (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Budget bowl of soup and bread at a Reykjavík café or self-cooked at resort (~1,200–1,800 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Reykjavík is very walkable. The city center is compact and most major attractions are within a 20–30 minute walk of each other. January weather in the city can be wet and windy — wear waterproof outer layers. The Hallgrímskirkja elevator is worth the small fee for the view.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Reykjanes Peninsula geothermal area — a landscape of steaming fumaroles, mud pots, and lava fields. Explore the Gunnuhver hot springs (free entry) — Iceland's largest mud pool, dramatically steaming in the cold air. Walk the marked paths carefully as the ground is extremely hot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Bridge Between Continents on the Reykjanes Peninsula — a footbridge spanning the rift between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Walking across is free. Nearby, visit the Reykjanesviti lighthouse, Iceland's oldest, perched on dramatic coastal cliffs. The entire peninsula is a UNESCO Global Geopark.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a warm dinner. The Reykjanes Peninsula is very close to the resort area and offers minimal light pollution — excellent for Northern Lights viewing. Set up in a field or coastal area and watch for auroras. The geothermal steam rising from the earth while auroras dance overhead is an unforgettable combination.

meals.breakfast: Skyr with honey and nuts at the resort (~500 ISK self-prepared)
meals.lunch: Thermos of homemade soup and rye bread sandwiches eaten at the Gunnuhver overlook (~600 ISK self-prepared)
meals.dinner: Lamb chops with roasted root vegetables — budget Icelandic comfort meal (~1,200 ISK self-cooked)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula has been highly volcanically active in recent years. Check for any volcanic alerts at vedur.is before visiting. The area is generally safe to visit but some roads may be closed near active eruption sites. Gunnuhver is extremely hot — stay strictly on marked paths.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free self-guided lava field walk near the resort. The Reykjanes Peninsula is covered in fascinating moss-covered lava fields — walk carefully and stay on paths to protect the fragile moss. Bring binoculars for birdwatching — Iceland has large populations of ravens, ptarmigan, and wintering seabirds in January.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local geothermal bakery if one is accessible in the area — some Icelandic bakers use geothermal heat to bake traditional rúgbrauð (hot spring rye bread) underground. Purchase a loaf (~600 ISK) and enjoy with Icelandic butter. Spend the afternoon at another local geothermal swimming pool for a long, relaxing soak.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated aurora photography evening. Set up at the beachfront or a dark coastal spot with a tripod. Use manual camera settings: ISO 800–3200, aperture f/2.8 or wider, shutter speed 5–25 seconds. Even a smartphone with a night mode can capture faint auroras. Stay out for 2–3 hours if conditions are favorable.

meals.breakfast: Rye bread with smoked trout and cream cheese (~700 ISK self-prepared)
meals.lunch: Fresh rúgbrauð with Icelandic butter and skyr at the pool café (~900 ISK)
meals.dinner: Pasta with creamy mushroom sauce and salad at the resort (~800 ISK self-cooked)

day_by_day.notes: Rúgbrauð (Icelandic geothermal rye bread) is dense, slightly sweet, and delicious. It's a must-try budget food experience. Geothermal swimming pools are the heart of Icelandic social life — don't miss the chance to soak in the hot pots and chat with locals.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Þórsmörk (Thorsmork) valley if road conditions permit — a stunning glacial valley surrounded by three glaciers. Access in January requires a super jeep or guided tour (~15,000–20,000 ISK) due to river crossings. Alternatively, explore the Hveragerði geothermal town, about 45 minutes from Reykjavík, which has a free geothermal park with hot springs and steaming vents.
day_by_day.afternoon: If visiting Hveragerði, hike the Reykjadalur (Steam Valley) trail — a 3.5 km hike to a natural hot river where you can bathe for free. The trail takes about 45 minutes each way. Bring a swimsuit and towel. This is one of Iceland's best free hot spring experiences. The trail can be icy — wear crampons.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort tired and happy after the hot river soak. Cook a filling dinner and rest. Check aurora forecast for the night — if KP index is 4 or above, make the effort to go out for a viewing session. Some of the most spectacular aurora displays happen on clear, cold January nights.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal with dried fruit and coffee at the resort (~500 ISK self-prepared)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the Reykjadalur hot river (~700 ISK self-prepared)
meals.dinner: Hearty vegetable and bean stew with crusty bread at the resort (~800 ISK self-cooked)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur hot river hike is one of Iceland's best free experiences. The hot river is warm enough to bathe in year-round. In January, the contrast of cold air and warm water is magical. The trail starts from Hveragerði town — parking is available at the trailhead. Check trail conditions before going.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at leisure — pack souvenirs, do laundry, and reflect on the trip. Visit a local Icelandic wool store (Álafoss in Mosfellsbær is a budget-friendly factory outlet) for affordable lopapeysa wool sweaters, mittens, and hats — genuine Icelandic wool products at lower prices than tourist shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final major activity: visit the Perlan Museum in Reykjavík (~2,900 ISK entry) — built on top of six geothermal hot water tanks. Features an indoor ice cave experience, Northern Lights planetarium show, and exhibits on Icelandic geology and nature. The observation deck offers 360-degree views of Reykjavík and surrounding mountains — free to access.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights hunting night. This is your last full night — make it count. Drive or walk to the darkest accessible spot near the resort. Bring hot chocolate in a thermos, warm blankets, and your camera. If the aurora is active, stay out as long as you can stand the cold. A green curtain dancing over the beachfront would be the perfect farewell from Iceland.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at a local café — eggs, skyr, rye bread, smoked salmon (~1,800 ISK) as a special treat
meals.lunch: Soup and bread at the Perlan café (~1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last night — fish stew or grilled Arctic char at a mid-range restaurant (~3,500–4,500 ISK) or a very special self-cooked meal with quality ingredients from the supermarket

day_by_day.notes: The Perlan Northern Lights show is a great backup if skies have been cloudy all trip — it gives you a simulated aurora experience inside. However, nothing compares to the real thing. Álafoss factory outlet is in Mosfellsbær, about 15 minutes from Reykjavík — great for authentic, reasonably priced Icelandic wool goods.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Wake up early for one last beachfront walk at the resort — breathe in the fresh Arctic air and take in the dramatic coastal scenery one last time. Pack all belongings, check out of the Aegean Bliss Resort, and store luggage if needed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, visit any remaining local spots near the resort. Stop at a local café for a final bowl of Icelandic soup or a skyr parfait. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs — Icelandic chocolate, dried fish (harðfiskur), or a small lava rock ornament from a budget shop.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Keflavík International Airport via the Flybus shuttle (~3,000 ISK). Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight. Reflect on 13 incredible days of Northern Lights, hot springs, waterfalls, glaciers, and one of the world's most unique landscapes. Iceland on a budget is absolutely possible — and unforgettable.

meals.breakfast: Final skyr with granola and Icelandic coffee at the resort or a nearby café (~700 ISK self-prepared)
meals.lunch: Hot dog at Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur in Reykjavík on the way to the airport if time permits (~500 ISK) or airport café (~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or onboard flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Book the Flybus return transfer in advance at re.is to guarantee a seat — flights from Keflavík depart throughout the day and the bus runs to match them. Allow extra time in January for potential road delays due to snow or ice. Double-check passport, boarding pass, and any duty-free purchases before security. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and collect luggage, then arrange airport transfer or rental car to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation. Step outside briefly to scan the sky for northern lights if energy permits.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In flight
meals.lunch: N/A - In flight
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at the airport or a 24-hour convenience store en route to the hotel (Noodle Station or a petrol station deli if open)

day_by_day.notes: January arrival means darkness and potential aurora activity immediately. Keep your eyes on the sky during the drive. Download the Vedur aurora forecast app before landing. Pack layers for the cold Icelandic January night (expect -2°C to 4°C).

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort. Take a short beachfront walk along the coastline to breathe in the crisp Atlantic air and orient yourself to the surroundings. Sunrise is not until around 11:00 in January, so enjoy the dramatic blue-hour light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a transfer into Reykjavik (approximately 45-60 minutes). Join the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour to explore the city's vibrant food scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr, lamb soup, and rye bread while learning about the city's history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area. After dinner, check the aurora forecast. If the KP index is favorable, step outside or drive to a dark spot near the resort for an impromptu northern lights viewing session.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort - enjoy the included or buffet spread
meals.lunch: Snacks and tastings included during the Food & Culture Walking Tour in Reykjavik
meals.dinner: Grillhúsið or Hamborgarabúllan in Reykjavik before heading back - mid-range burgers and Icelandic grill fare around 2,500-4,000 ISK per person

day_by_day.notes: The Food & Culture Walking Tour typically runs 3-4 hours. Book in advance. Dress in warm waterproof layers - January in Reykjavik is cold and often windy. Sunset is around 16:00 so the city will be dark by mid-afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, head to the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa, which is conveniently located near Keflavik and easily accessible from the resort. Arrive early (pre-book the 10:00 slot) to enjoy the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters before crowds build. Enjoy the in-water silica mud masks and mineral-rich steam.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue your Blue Lagoon experience through the afternoon. Upgrade to the Comfort package if budget allows for access to a private changing area and a drink at the in-water bar. Depart by 15:00 and return to the resort to warm up and relax.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep - join the small-group guided jeep tour departing in the evening (typically 20:00-23:00). Expert guides will drive away from Reykjavik's light pollution into the dark Icelandic countryside to maximize aurora viewing chances.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: LAVA Restaurant inside Blue Lagoon - splurge slightly on the iconic setting; fish soup and open-faced sandwiches around 3,500-5,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Light early dinner at the resort or a nearby grill before the night jeep tour - keep it simple so you're ready for a late evening

day_by_day.notes: Pre-booking Blue Lagoon is absolutely mandatory - slots sell out weeks in advance. The Comfort package (around 12,000 ISK) includes towel, one drink, and silica mud mask. The Jeep Northern Lights tour typically costs 10,000-15,000 ISK per person. Guides will monitor aurora forecasts in real time.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after the late-night aurora tour. Enjoy a slow breakfast and review photos from the previous evening. Check aurora forecasts for the coming nights. Take a leisurely walk along the beachfront near the resort and explore the immediate coastal surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the famous Golden Circle route (self-drive or guided day tour). Start with Þingvellir National Park - walk between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates and explore the historic Viking parliament site. Continue to the Geysir Geothermal Area to watch Strokkur erupt every 5-10 minutes.
day_by_day.evening: Complete the Golden Circle with a visit to Gullfoss Waterfall, dramatically lit by car headlights and moonlight in winter. Return to the resort by 20:00. Check aurora forecast and spend time on the hotel terrace or beach if lights appear.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Geysir Center cafeteria near the geyser area - lamb soup and Icelandic bread around 2,000-3,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn on the Golden Circle route - cozy mid-range Icelandic cuisine, around 4,000-6,000 ISK per person

day_by_day.notes: Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip. Roads may be icy in January - check road conditions at road.is before departing. Rent a 4WD if possible. Dress in full winter gear as outdoor stops will be very cold and windy.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak in Flúðir, Iceland's oldest natural swimming pool dating to 1891. The drive from the resort takes about 1.5 hours. Arrive when it opens (typically 10:00) for a peaceful soak in the rustic geothermal pool surrounded by geysers and steam vents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Flúðir and the surrounding countryside. Visit the local mushroom farm or greenhouse (Icelandic greenhouses are geothermally heated). Begin the drive back toward the resort, stopping at any scenic viewpoints along the route.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Enjoy a relaxing dinner and another northern lights watch session. January offers the longest nights of the year with maximum darkness - prime aurora hunting conditions.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Minilik Ethiopian Restaurant or local soup café in Flúðir village - simple and warming around 2,000-3,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort or a nearby coastal restaurant - fresh Icelandic fish dishes around 4,000-6,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon entry is around 3,000 ISK per adult - much more affordable than Blue Lagoon and equally magical. Bring your own towel or rent one on site. The pool is outdoors at approximately 38-40°C, perfect for a cold January day. Swimwear is required.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip along the South Coast. Depart early and drive east along Route 1 to Seljalandsfoss waterfall, where you can walk behind the cascading water (note: the path behind may be icy and closed in winter - check conditions). Continue to Skógafoss waterfall for dramatic rainbow views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík. Marvel at the dramatic basalt column formations and sea stacks. Visit the iconic Reynisdrangar sea stacks. Explore the village of Vík and its red-roofed church. Begin the drive back westward.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at Seljavallalaug, one of Iceland's oldest swimming pools (free entry), on the way back if time and conditions permit. Return to resort for dinner and aurora watching. The South Coast's open skies offer excellent northern lights viewing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort - pack snacks for the road
meals.lunch: Skál! Eatery in Vík - hearty lamb burger and fish and chips, mid-range around 3,000-4,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Strondin Bistro Bar near the resort area or hotel restaurant - fresh catch of the day around 4,500-6,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast drive is approximately 350 km round trip. Road conditions in January can be challenging - monitor road.is closely. Reynisfjara beach has dangerous sneaker waves - never turn your back on the ocean. Dress in full waterproof gear.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Spend the morning relaxing at the resort's facilities. If the resort has a hot tub or spa, indulge in a morning soak. Organize photos and journals from the first week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjanes Peninsula, close to the resort. Explore the Bridge Between Continents (a symbolic walkway between tectonic plates), the Gunnuhver hot spring mud pools, and the Reykjanes Lighthouse - one of Iceland's oldest. The entire peninsula is a UNESCO Global Geopark.
day_by_day.evening: Second Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep tour (book a second night if the first was cloudy or if you want to maximize chances). Alternatively, self-drive to a dark location on the Reykjanes Peninsula with a clear sky forecast for aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Café Bryggjan in Grindavík - traditional Icelandic fish soup and langoustine, beloved local spot around 2,500-4,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Við Fjöruna Seafood Restaurant in Hafnarfjörður - fresh Icelandic seafood in a cozy setting around 4,500-7,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is extremely geothermally active. Stay on marked paths near Gunnuhver as the ground can be unstable. The area around Grindavík has seen volcanic activity in recent years - check local advisories before visiting. The peninsula is very close to the resort, making it an ideal low-effort day.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Snæfellsnes Peninsula (longer drive, approximately 2.5 hours from the resort). Depart early to maximize the limited daylight. Visit Snæfellsjökull National Park, the glacier volcano made famous by Jules Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Snæfellsnes highlights: Kirkjufell mountain (Iceland's most photographed peak), Arnarstapi coastal cliffs with dramatic basalt formations, and the charming fishing village of Stykkishólmur. The volcanic landscape is otherworldly in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back to the resort. The long drive back offers excellent open-sky aurora viewing opportunities from the car. Pull over safely if lights appear. Arrive back at resort by 21:00-22:00.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort - pack a hearty meal for the long day
meals.lunch: Narfeyrarstofa Restaurant in Stykkishólmur - fresh seafood and Icelandic lamb in a historic building, around 4,000-6,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Late dinner at the hotel restaurant or a quick stop at a petrol station grill on Route 1 returning

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day - approximately 400+ km round trip. Start no later than 09:00 to make the most of the 5-6 hours of daylight. Road conditions on the Snæfellsnes Peninsula can be severe in January. A 4WD vehicle is strongly recommended. Consider an organized day tour if uncomfortable driving in winter conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning after the long Snæfellsnes day. Leisurely breakfast and spa time at the resort. If the resort has a geothermal pool or hot tub, spend the morning soaking and relaxing. Review the week's photos and plan the remaining days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Reykjavik for culture and exploration. Tour Hallgrímskirkja church (take the elevator to the top for panoramic city views), explore the Harpa Concert Hall architecture, and browse the Laugavegur shopping street for Icelandic wool sweaters and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Reykjavik's nightlife and dining scene. Explore the Laugavegur bar and restaurant strip. Return to resort by 23:00 or stay overnight in Reykjavik if preferred (optional).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) in Reykjavik harbor - famous lobster soup and grilled fish skewers, budget-friendly around 2,000-3,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Snaps Bistro Bar in Reykjavik - French-Icelandic fusion, popular mid-range spot around 4,500-7,000 ISK per person

day_by_day.notes: Hallgrímskirkja tower elevator costs around 1,000 ISK. Harpa Concert Hall has free public access to the lobby and lower floors. January is low season in Reykjavik so restaurants are less crowded and some may have off-season deals. The Laugavegur street is walkable and compact.

day_by_day.morning: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike preparation day - note that Landmannalaugar is typically inaccessible by standard vehicles in January due to deep snow and closed highland roads (F-roads). Instead, explore the Hengill geothermal area near Hveragerði, which offers accessible hot spring hiking year-round.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Reykjadalur Hot Spring River trail from Hveragerði (approximately 1.5 hours each way). This moderate hike leads to a natural hot spring river where you can bathe in geothermally heated water flowing through a valley - a stunning and accessible alternative to Landmannalaugar in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort after the hike. Warm up with a hot shower and dinner. Check aurora forecast for an evening lights watch from the resort's beachfront - the open ocean horizon provides unobstructed northern sky views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Ölverk Pizza & Brewery in Hveragerði - craft beer and wood-fired pizza in a geothermally heated brewery, around 3,000-4,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort - reward yourself after the hike with a warm Icelandic lamb stew

day_by_day.notes: IMPORTANT: Landmannalaugar F-roads (F208, F224) are closed in January and inaccessible without a specially equipped super jeep expedition. The Reykjadalur trail is an excellent substitute. Bring a change of clothes and a dry bag for the hot spring river swim. The trail can be icy - bring traction devices for boots.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Kerið volcanic crater lake, a stunning 3,000-year-old caldera with vivid red and black volcanic rock contrasting with the turquoise lake below. Dramatic in winter with possible snow coverage. Easy walk around the rim (about 30 minutes). Combine with a visit to nearby Skálholt Cathedral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Laugarvatn Fontana Geothermal Baths on the shores of Lake Laugarvatn. These modern baths offer steam rooms built directly over natural geothermal vents, outdoor geothermal pools, and a unique experience of baking traditional Icelandic rye bread in the ground using geothermal heat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a final aurora hunting session. This being the penultimate full evening, make the most of the darkness. Set an alarm for 23:00 and 02:00 to check the sky if aurora activity is forecasted. The beachfront location provides an ideal dark horizon.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn - Arctic char and lamb dishes with lake views, mid-range around 4,000-6,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort or self-catering with Icelandic groceries from Krónan supermarket

day_by_day.notes: Kerið crater entry fee is approximately 700 ISK. Laugarvatn Fontana entry is around 4,200 ISK per adult. The rye bread tasting experience is included with entry. Both are excellent value. This is a relaxed day designed to balance the more intense earlier days.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day - morning soak at the Blue Lagoon (book a second visit or visit for the first time if Day 3 was too rushed). Alternatively, enjoy the resort's own facilities for a slow morning. Pack non-essential items and prepare bags for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik for final souvenir shopping on Laugavegur and Skólavörðustígur streets. Pick up Icelandic wool products (lopapeysa sweaters), local liquors (Brennivín), lava salt, and Icelandic chocolate. Visit the Settlement Exhibition museum for a final dose of Viking history.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Reykjavik. Splurge slightly on a memorable final meal. Return to Aegean Bliss Resort for the last night. Set alarms for a final aurora watch attempt - this is your last chance for the trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Messinn Restaurant in Reykjavik - pan-fried fish of the day in cast iron skillets, beloved local institution around 3,500-5,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) in Reykjavik - upscale Icelandic ingredients in a lively atmosphere, slight splurge at 7,000-10,000 ISK per person

day_by_day.notes: Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) entry is around 2,200 ISK. Laugavegur shops are generally open until 18:00-20:00. Book the farewell dinner reservation in advance as popular Reykjavik restaurants fill up even in January. Keep receipts for VAT tax refund at the airport (minimum purchase thresholds apply).

day_by_day.morning: Final morning - enjoy a last hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort. Take a final beachfront walk and soak in the Icelandic coastal scenery. Check out of the hotel and load the car. Allow 45-60 minutes to drive to Keflavik International Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavik Airport with ample time (minimum 2.5-3 hours before international departure). Process VAT refunds at the airport refund desk before check-in if eligible. Browse duty-free for final Icelandic spirits, chocolates, and skincare products from the Blue Lagoon line.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with memories of glowing auroras, steaming hot springs, volcanic landscapes, and the magic of the midnight darkness. Safe travels.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Keflavik Airport restaurants - Islenski Barinn or Pylsuvagninn for a final Icelandic hot dog (pylsa) around 800-1,500 ISK
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time and work backwards to calculate hotel checkout. Most Icelandic hotels allow late checkout until 12:00 - request this if your flight is in the afternoon or evening. Return rental car with a full tank of petrol (gas stations near the airport include N1 and Orkan). The airport VAT refund desk is located before security - have all receipts and passport ready.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the dark countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to chase the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to maximize your chances of witnessing the phenomenon. Hot chocolate and warm blankets included.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, a silica mud mask ritual, and a swim-up bar with Icelandic craft beer. A quintessential hot spring experience set against dramatic lava fields.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest natural swimming pool, a rustic geothermal hot spring dating back to 1891. Watch small geysers bubble nearby while soaking under open skies. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and wonderfully authentic.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and Viking heritage on a guided walking tour. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup, fermented shark, and fresh langoustine. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and the colorful old harbour district.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's breathtaking rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a natural geothermal hot spring soak at the end of the trail. Witness vivid green, red, and yellow volcanic landscapes unlike anywhere else on Earth.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30 — No morning activities scheduled. Late-night private transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities scheduled due to late-night arrival.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer from Keflavik Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unwind in your beachfront suite, and enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the resort. Light late-night room service available.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort — request the chef's selection of Icelandic smoked lamb, skyr parfait, and warm Icelandic bread with cultured butter

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is at 22:30 local time. Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. Immigration and baggage claim may take 45–60 minutes. Resort should be notified of late check-in in advance. Rest well — the itinerary begins in earnest tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late start — enjoy a luxurious breakfast at the resort's oceanfront dining room. Take a slow orientation walk along the beachfront grounds of Aegean Bliss Resort, breathing in the crisp Arctic air and acclimating to Iceland's winter light (sunrise around 11:00 AM in January).
day_by_day.afternoon: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa: A private transfer takes you to Iceland's most iconic geothermal destination. Soak in the signature milky-blue silica-rich waters, indulge in an in-water silica mud mask ritual, and book a premium Retreat Spa treatment — choose from a lava scrub, algae wrap, or floating massage. Enjoy the exclusive Retreat Lounge with Champagne service.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset cocktail hour at the bar overlooking the beachfront. Dine at the resort's flagship restaurant featuring locally sourced Icelandic cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — full Icelandic breakfast spread: fresh skyr, smoked Arctic char, rye bread, Icelandic cheeses, and hot porridge with bilberry jam
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant — in-spa dining with langoustine soup, Icelandic flatbread, and grilled fish of the day
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort flagship restaurant — pan-seared cod with beurre blanc, roasted root vegetables, and a selection from the Icelandic wine and spirits list

day_by_day.notes: Book Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa packages well in advance — premium slots fill quickly. January daylight is limited to roughly 5–6 hours; the Blue Lagoon is magical in the dark with steam rising from the heated waters. Keep an eye on northern lights forecasts for tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour: A private guide meets you for a bespoke morning exploration of Reykjavik's compact but vibrant city center. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church, stroll Laugavegur street, and discover Viking heritage at key cultural landmarks including the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the food and culture experience with tastings at artisan spots — try traditional hákarl (fermented shark) for the adventurous, fresh langoustine bisque, Icelandic lamb skewers, and hand-rolled licorice chocolates. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall for its stunning geometric glass architecture overlooking the harbor. Browse premium Icelandic design boutiques for wool sweaters and volcanic jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep: As darkness falls, your expert guide picks you up in a premium 4x4 jeep and drives into the dark countryside far from Reykjavik's light pollution. Wrap in provided thermal blankets and hot cocoa as you scan the skies for the Aurora Borealis. Photography assistance included.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh juice, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Matur og Drykkur, Reykjavik — a celebrated restaurant serving elevated traditional Icelandic cuisine including cod head, salted cod, and skyr desserts
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavik — Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant offering a Nordic tasting menu with wine pairings; reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Northern Lights activity is weather and aurora-activity dependent. The guide monitors forecasts in real time and selects the optimal dark-sky location on the night. Dress in maximum thermal layers — temperatures can drop to -10°C or below. Most jeep tours last 3–4 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the resort. Enjoy a spa session at Aegean Bliss Resort's wellness facilities — geothermal pool, sauna, and steam room. Optional: sunrise yoga class (around 11:00 AM) offered by the resort overlooking the beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak: Private transfer to Flúðir village to visit Iceland's oldest natural swimming pool, dating back to 1891. This rustic, authentic geothermal experience contrasts beautifully with the Blue Lagoon — surrounded by bubbling hot springs, geysers, and a wild natural landscape. Enjoy a long, peaceful soak in the 38–40°C waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a private in-suite dining experience — the resort chef prepares a curated four-course Icelandic dinner delivered directly to your beachfront suite with candles, local flowers, and a bottle of premium Champagne.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — Icelandic skyr bowls with granola, fresh berries, and honey; freshly baked pastries and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet basket prepared by the resort chef and enjoyed near the Secret Lagoon — smoked lamb wraps, artisan cheeses, fruit, and thermos of hot soup
meals.dinner: Private in-suite dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — langoustine bisque, slow-roasted Icelandic lamb with root vegetable purée, and skyr panna cotta with crowberry coulis

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is about 1.5 hours from Reykjavik. January conditions make the drive scenic but potentially icy — ensure a professional driver is arranged. The lagoon is far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and offers an intimate, authentic experience. Bring a swimsuit and towel, though rentals are available.

day_by_day.morning: Golden Circle Private Tour — Morning departure with a luxury private guide. First stop: Þingvellir (Thingvellir) National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk through the dramatic Almannagjá rift valley and learn about Iceland's ancient parliament, the Alþingi, established in 930 AD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle: Visit the Geysir Geothermal Area to witness Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 30 meters into the air. Then proceed to the majestic Gullfoss Waterfall — one of Europe's most powerful cascades, partially frozen in January and extraordinarily dramatic. Enjoy the raw, elemental power of Iceland's landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep (second opportunity): Weather permitting, your guide takes you to a dark-sky location near the Golden Circle area for a prime aurora viewing opportunity before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — full hot breakfast with Icelandic oatmeal, smoked fish platter, and freshly baked rye bread
meals.lunch: Geysir Center Restaurant — hearty Icelandic lamb soup, fresh bread, and Icelandic dairy dessert
meals.dinner: Friðheimar Tomato Farm Restaurant, Reykholt — a unique dining experience inside a geothermally heated greenhouse; tomato-based menu with fresh tomato soup, bruschetta, and pasta, paired with their house tomato-infused Bloody Mary

day_by_day.notes: January Golden Circle roads can be icy and require 4x4 vehicles. Dress in full winter gear. Gullfoss is partially frozen in January and extraordinarily beautiful — allow extra time for photography. Friðheimar requires advance reservations and is a truly unique Iceland dining experience not to be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Snæfellsnes Peninsula Private Day Tour — Depart early for the dramatic Snæfellsnes Peninsula, home to the iconic Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano (immortalized in Jules Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth). Drive through lava fields, past black sand beaches, and along towering sea cliffs with stunning Atlantic Ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming fishing village of Arnarstapi with its dramatic basalt arch formations and colony of Arctic birds. Visit Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach with its shipwreck remnants and volcanic rock formations. Continue to Kirkjufell mountain — one of Iceland's most photographed peaks — for a scenic stop and photography session.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to the resort. Enjoy a relaxing evening in the resort's geothermal pool under the open sky, watching for northern lights with a glass of Icelandic craft beer or Brennivín schnapps.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — continental Icelandic spread with cold cuts, cheeses, smoked salmon, and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Hotel Búðir Restaurant, Snæfellsnes — one of Iceland's most romantic and celebrated remote restaurants; fresh Atlantic fish, lamb, and locally foraged ingredients
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort — three-course dinner at the main restaurant; grilled Arctic char with dill cream sauce, roasted potatoes, and a warm chocolate lava cake with skyr ice cream

day_by_day.notes: The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is approximately 2 hours from Reykjavik. January driving conditions require a professional driver and 4x4 vehicle. Hotel Búðir requires advance reservations — it is a remote, iconic dining location. The peninsula is known as 'Iceland in miniature' as it showcases nearly all of Iceland's landscape types.

day_by_day.morning: Midpoint rest day — sleep in and enjoy a long spa morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Book a signature 90-minute volcanic stone massage or geothermal body wrap treatment. Lounge in the resort's heated infinity pool overlooking the beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reykjavik Art and Design Afternoon: Private cultural tour of Reykjavik's premier galleries and museums. Visit the National Museum of Iceland for deep Viking and Norse history, then explore the Reykjavik Art Museum's Hafnarhús building. Browse Kolaportið flea market if open, and visit premium Icelandic design stores for bespoke souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep (third opportunity): A dedicated evening aurora chase with your expert guide. January offers long, dark nights — prime northern lights season. Tonight's chase ventures further into the countryside for maximum dark-sky conditions.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — eggs any style, fresh-pressed Icelandic berry juices, smoked lamb, and artisan toast
meals.lunch: Kopar Restaurant, Reykjavik Old Harbour — fresh seafood in a converted warehouse overlooking the harbor; lobster tails, oysters, and fish of the day
meals.dinner: Grillið Restaurant, Radisson Blu Saga Hotel, Reykjavik — rooftop fine dining with panoramic city views; Icelandic beef tenderloin, truffle risotto, and an extensive Nordic wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: This is a built-in recovery and flexibility day. If previous northern lights hunts were unsuccessful due to weather, tonight is another prime opportunity. January aurora activity is statistically high. The KP index and cloud forecasts should be monitored throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: South Coast Private Tour — Depart for Iceland's legendary South Coast. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall, where in summer you can walk behind the curtain of water; in January the frozen formations are spectacular and otherworldly. Continue to Skógafoss, one of Iceland's largest and most powerful waterfalls, with a rainbow visible on clear days even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the black sand beach of Reynisfjara, one of the world's most dramatic beaches with towering basalt column cliffs, sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), and thunderous Atlantic waves. Visit the nearby village of Vík í Mýrdal — Iceland's southernmost village — for a warm drink and a look at the iconic black church. Continue to Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon if time permits for an awe-inspiring view of floating blue icebergs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Celebratory mid-trip dinner at the resort's finest dining setting — request a private beachfront table if weather permits, with a bonfire and stargazing service arranged by the concierge.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — hot porridge with Icelandic honey, smoked fish, fresh pastries, and hot coffee
meals.lunch: Pakkhús Restaurant, Höfn — if extending to Jökulsárlón area; renowned for fresh Höfn langoustine — the best in Iceland; langoustine tails in garlic butter with homemade bread
meals.dinner: Private beachfront dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — five-course tasting menu with Champagne: langoustine, smoked lamb, Icelandic cheese course, and a skyr soufflé

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast is approximately 2–3 hours from Reykjavik. Reynisfjara beach has dangerous sneaker waves — stay well back from the water's edge and follow all guide instructions. Jökulsárlón is 4.5 hours from Reykjavik — if included, this is a very full day; consider an overnight in the area or adjust the itinerary. January conditions make icy road driving essential with a professional driver.

day_by_day.morning: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike (Highland Adventure): Depart with a private highland guide in a specially equipped super-jeep for the Landmannalaugar highlands. Trek through Iceland's breathtaking rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains — vivid greens, reds, yellows, and purples contrasting with snow and lava fields. This is one of Iceland's most visually stunning landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the Landmannalaugar geothermal hot spring area. After the invigorating hike through volcanic terrain, reward yourself with a long soak in the natural hot spring where geothermal water mixes with cold mountain streams to create a perfect temperature. This wild, remote bathing experience is utterly unique.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort via super-jeep. Enjoy a restorative evening in the resort spa — sauna, steam room, and geothermal pool. Early dinner and rest after the day's adventure.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — high-energy breakfast: Icelandic oatmeal with nuts and berries, protein-rich smoked fish, and strong coffee for the hiking day ahead
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet highland lunch prepared by the resort — artisan sandwiches with Icelandic lamb and cheese, energy bars, dried fruit, and a thermos of hearty lamb soup
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort — lighter recovery dinner: pan-seared salmon with lemon herb butter, roasted vegetables, and warm Icelandic bread pudding with vanilla cream

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar is only accessible in winter via super-jeep with highly experienced highland guides — standard vehicles cannot reach this area in January. The highland roads (F-roads) are closed to normal traffic. Dress in full waterproof hiking gear with thermal layers. Bring a swimsuit for the hot spring soak. This is one of the most extraordinary experiences in Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Private Glacier Walk on Sólheimajökull: Depart with a certified glacier guide for a premium private glacier walk on Sólheimajökull, an outlet glacier of the massive Mýrdalsjökull ice cap. Don crampons and harness for an intimate guided walk across blue ice formations, exploring crevasses, ice caves, and dramatic meltwater channels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ice Cave Exploration: Visit a natural ice cave inside a glacier (subject to guide safety assessment and conditions). The electric blue ice formations inside these caves are among Iceland's most surreal and photogenic natural wonders. A private guide ensures an exclusive, unhurried experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Enjoy a long, hot geothermal soak in the resort's outdoor pool as the northern lights potentially dance overhead. Celebrate the day's adventures with a premium cocktail at the resort bar.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — full hot breakfast with scrambled eggs, Icelandic sausages, smoked salmon, and fresh-baked bread
meals.lunch: Skógarfoss Café area — hearty lamb stew and Icelandic brown bread near the South Coast glacier region
meals.dinner: The Farm Restaurant (Rauðaskriða), South Iceland — rustic-luxe farm-to-table dining; slow-cooked Icelandic lamb, root vegetable gratin, and homemade ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Ice cave availability is subject to guide safety assessment — conditions change daily in January. Natural ice caves are most stable and accessible in winter (November–March), making this the ideal season. Glacier walks require moderate fitness. All equipment (crampons, harness, helmet) is provided. Photography is exceptional inside blue ice caves — bring a wide-angle lens.

day_by_day.morning: Private Whale Watching and Puffin Boat Tour from Reykjavik Old Harbour: Board a premium small-group whale watching vessel from Reykjavik's harbor. January offers opportunities to spot humpback whales, minke whales, and dolphins in Faxaflói Bay. Warm onboard with hot chocolate and Icelandic pastries provided. Expert marine biologist guide narrates throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik for a premium afternoon: Visit the Perlan Museum — a stunning glass-domed building on Öskjuhlíð hill offering a real indoor ice cave exhibit, northern lights planetarium show, and panoramic 360° views of Reykjavik and surrounding mountains. Enjoy Champagne at the Perlan observation deck.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep: A dedicated premium aurora chase to maximize the chance of witnessing the northern lights before the trip concludes. Your expert guide selects the best location based on real-time KP index and cloud cover forecasts.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — smoked fish platter, Icelandic rye bread with butter and cheese, fresh fruit, and hot coffee
meals.lunch: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron), Reykjavik Old Harbour — a legendary local institution; famous lobster soup and grilled fish skewers in a rustic harbourside setting
meals.dinner: Óx Restaurant, Reykjavik — an intimate, reservation-only counter dining experience with a 12-course Nordic tasting menu; one of Reykjavik's most exclusive and celebrated dining experiences

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching in January is weather dependent — tours may be cancelled in rough seas. A reputable operator with a warm onboard vessel is essential. Óx Restaurant requires booking months in advance and accommodates very few guests per seating — confirm reservation well before the trip. This is one of the most exclusive dining experiences in Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Blue Lagoon Return — Premium Retreat Experience: A second visit to the Blue Lagoon, this time booking the full Retreat Spa package — access to the exclusive underground Retreat Spa, private lagoon section, floating breakfast in the water, and a signature ritual treatment (lava scrub, algae wrap, or sound bath). This elevated experience is distinct from the standard lagoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort for a leisurely afternoon. Final souvenir shopping at the resort boutique — Icelandic wool blankets, volcanic salt, artisan skincare products made from Icelandic glacial water and algae. Enjoy a final afternoon tea service at the resort lounge.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — a special seven-course tasting menu arranged by the resort's head chef celebrating the finest Icelandic ingredients: langoustine, wild salmon, Icelandic lamb, skyr, and seasonal foraged elements. Paired with premium Icelandic and international wines.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — celebratory late breakfast with Champagne, smoked salmon Benedict, fresh pastries, and Icelandic fruit preserves
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa — exclusive in-water floating lunch service: fresh langoustine rolls, Champagne, and seasonal Icelandic bites
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort — seven-course farewell tasting menu with wine pairing: langoustine tartare, smoked lamb consommé, Arctic char crudo, Icelandic beef tenderloin, artisan cheese course, skyr soufflé, and petit fours

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa is the premium tier above the standard lagoon — it includes an exclusive underground spa with private lagoon access, flotation pools, and bespoke treatments. Book the floating breakfast in advance as slots are extremely limited. This is the perfect penultimate day luxury experience before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort — leisurely breakfast and a last walk along the beachfront. Pack and check out. Arrange for resort staff to store luggage while you enjoy final moments. Optional: a final short soak in the resort's geothermal outdoor pool as a last Icelandic memory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: Optional final Reykjavik stroll along the harbor, visit to the Sun Voyager sculpture (Sólfar) for photographs, and last-minute shopping on Laugavegur. Private luxury transfer to Keflavik International Airport with ample time for premium lounge access and duty-free shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavik International Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of northern lights, geothermal wonders, volcanic landscapes, glacier adventures, and world-class Icelandic cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — final full Icelandic breakfast: skyr with berries, smoked fish, fresh pastries, Icelandic butter, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Keflavik Airport Premium Lounge or Reykjavik café — fresh Icelandic soup, open-faced sandwiches, and Icelandic pastries
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal — carry Icelandic chocolates and skyr snacks purchased at duty-free as a final taste of Iceland

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight time and arrange airport transfer at least 3 hours before scheduled departure to account for January weather delays and airport processing. Keflavik Airport has a good duty-free selection of Icelandic spirits (Brennivín, Icelandic vodka), chocolates, skincare, and wool goods. Ensure all resort charges are settled the evening before for a smooth departure morning.
